sources.title: Jane Doe interview transcript
sources.text:
[Illustrative transcript. Fictional SME. Session ses:jane-2025-01-15, Critical Decision Method.]

Interviewer: Walk me through the first thing you look at.
Jane: Score first, always. Anything at 750 or above is prime and I approve it outright; I'm about 98 percent sure on those.
Interviewer: And below 750?
Jane: 650 is my floor for the standard tier. Under 650 we're in subprime territory and it's a different conversation.
Interviewer: What comes after score?
Jane: Debt-to-income. I take total monthly debt payments divided by gross monthly income. For standard tier I want DTI at 43 percent or lower.
Interviewer: Employment?
Jane: Two years in the current job is my minimum for standard.
Jane: Then inquiries. One hard inquiry in six months is normal life. More than one and the file goes conditional, I'd put myself at 75 percent: I ask them to explain the inquiries and I usually offer a smaller amount.
Jane: Three or more hard inquiries in six months and I read it as desperation for credit. I reject unless there's a strong compensating factor.
Jane: If everything clears, score at or above 650, DTI at or under 43, two years on the job, at most one inquiry, it's a standard approval and I'm 92 percent sure.
Interviewer: Anything that softens a borderline file?
Jane: Savings. Six months of expenses in the bank and I take about ten percent off my risk read. It's their safety net if the job goes.
Jane: Medical debt I only count at half toward DTI. People pay medical bills off; card debt means they overspend.
Jane: Married co-applicants are more stable than couples who are just dating, so I lean on a spouse's income more.
Jane: Young people, say 25 to 35, with income climbing fast, I'll approve even with a lower score.
Interviewer: Bankruptcy?
Jane: If the discharge was seven or more years ago and the rest of the file is strong, it's approvable. The Fair Credit Reporting Act says bankruptcies drop off after seven years anyway.
Interviewer: What don't you decide?
Jane: Rates. I never set the interest rate; pricing is a separate desk and I stay out of it.

sources.title: Sam Rivera interview transcript
sources.text:
[Illustrative transcript. Fictional SME. Session ses:sam-2025-02-03, Applied Cognitive Task Analysis.]

Interviewer: Where do junior underwriters get self-employed applicants wrong?
Sam: They read year-to-date or the 1099s. For self-employed income I use the two-year average from the tax returns, nothing else.
Sam: And the two-year job rule doesn't apply to them as written. I want three years of self-employment history before I treat it like a W-2 job.

concepts.label: Credit score
concepts.definition: Bureau credit score on the 300 to 850 FICO scale.

concepts.label: Debt-to-income ratio
concepts.definition: Total monthly debt payments divided by gross monthly income.

concepts.label: Monthly debt payments
concepts.definition: Sum of required monthly payments on all debts.

concepts.label: Hard inquiry
concepts.definition: A lender credit pull triggered by an application, counted over the last six months.

concepts.label: Savings buffer
concepts.definition: Months of expenses held in liquid savings.

concepts.label: Co-applicant
concepts.definition: A second applicant whose income and obligations are part of the application.

concepts.label: Bankruptcy
concepts.definition: A court-discharged insolvency on the applicant's record.

concepts.label: Self-employment income
concepts.definition: Income from the applicant's own business.

concepts.label: Approval tier
concepts.definition: Decision outcome: PRIME, STANDARD, CONDITIONAL, SUBPRIME or DENY.

concepts.label: Interest rate pricing
concepts.definition: Setting the rate and price terms for an approved loan.

claims.statement: A credit score of 750 or above qualifies as prime tier and is approved outright.
650 is the minimum credit score for the standard tier; below 650 is subprime.
Debt-to-income (DTI) is total monthly debt payments divided by gross monthly income.
For the standard tier, DTI must be 43% or lower.
claims.review_note: 43% mirrors the original General QM DTI cap. That cap was replaced by a price-based test in the 2020 ATR/QM amendments; keep as an internal credit policy, not a regulatory requirement.

claims.statement: Standard tier requires at least two years in the current job.
With more than one hard inquiry in six months, an otherwise standard file becomes CONDITIONAL at about 75% confidence: ask for an explanation of the inquiries and offer a smaller amount.
Three or more hard inquiries in six months signals credit desperation; reject unless there is a strong compensating factor.
Score of 650 or more, DTI of 43% or less, two or more years employed, and at most one hard inquiry is a STANDARD approval at about 92% confidence.
Six or more months of expenses in savings reduces the risk assessment by about 10%.
Medical debt counts at 50% toward DTI.
claims.review_note: Extracted, not yet confirmed. Needs SME confirmation and a check against how bureaus already treat medical collections.

claims.statement: Married co-applicants are treated as more stable than unmarried partners, so a spouse's income is weighted more heavily.
claims.review_note: Blocked: ECOA / Regulation B prohibits discrimination on the basis of marital status.

claims.statement: Applicants aged 25 to 35 with fast-rising income can be approved with a lower score.
claims.review_note: Blocked: ECOA / Regulation B restricts the use of age in credit decisions. Re-elicit as an income-trajectory signal with no age term.

claims.statement: A bankruptcy discharged seven or more years ago is approvable when the rest of the file is strong.
Under the FCRA, bankruptcies stop being reported after seven years.
claims.review_note: Blocked as a factual misstatement: FCRA section 605(a)(1) allows bankruptcy cases to be reported for up to ten years. The 7-year edge case itself stays valid as policy.

claims.statement: For self-employed applicants, income is the two-year average from tax returns, not year-to-date figures or 1099s.
Self-employed applicants need three years of self-employment history in place of the two-year job minimum.
This expertise does not cover setting interest rates or loan pricing.

regulations.label: Equal Credit Opportunity Act / Regulation B
regulations.description: Prohibits credit discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, or age (with limited exceptions), among other bases.

regulations.label: Fair Credit Reporting Act section 605
regulations.description: Limits how long adverse information can be reported: bankruptcy cases up to 10 years, most other adverse items 7 years.

regulations.label: Regulation Z Ability-to-Repay / Qualified Mortgage rule
regulations.description: Requires a reasonable, good-faith determination of ability to repay for covered mortgages. The General QM definition moved from a 43% DTI cap to a price-based test in the 2020 amendments.

steps.label: Two or more years employed (three if self-employed)?
At most one hard inquiry in six months?
